statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 13% (low), Stress 51% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Elevated attention is flagged for the 19:00-21:00 UTC pre-holiday close window. CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which no live price path exists until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, and Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash session is Tuesday 8 September.
headline: Nasdaq-100 back to unchanged after a full intraday round trip; a falling VIX and an orderly curve keep Tail low into the pre-holiday close
body: The August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 56,000 expected, with unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% m/m to $37.75. September Fed hike pricing moved to about 60%, yet transmission has stayed orderly: the 10-year is 4.78%, up about one basis point on the day, and the 2-year sits near 4.39%. The Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and has recovered to 29,481.00 against a 29,482.32 prior close. That is a path in which retracements are repeatedly occurring in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure this Tail score measures. Volatility confirms it: VIX is 14.10, down 1.54%, inside a 13.80-14.36 range. Internals are unusually split rather than aligned. Semiconductors are firm, with Micron, AMD, Arm and Intel all higher, while Apple, Microsoft and Tesla are lower and Tesla is down about 6% on an NHTSA audit query into Cybercab self-certification. Lululemon fell sharply on a second guidance cut, a consumer read rather than a Nasdaq-100 driver. That dispersion keeps the index flat while the broader composite is modestly lower, and dispersion of this kind is mean-reversion friendly at index level. Delayed shared cross-asset context is consistent: index futures marginally lower, VIX futures lower, Treasury futures little changed and gold weaker, with no single aligned direction. Oil is quiet at $91.19 WTI and $96.00 Brent despite unresolved US-Iran hostilities and reduced Strait of Hormuz transits, which remain a standing rather than a freshly escalating premium. Stress stays elevated because the hawkish repricing, the geopolitical backdrop and the single-name damage are all real, but none of them has produced the price-path behaviour that Tail is defined to capture. The near-term structural fact dominates the forecast: US cash closes at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which the remainder of this horizon is a halted market with no live price path.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours cover a calm overnight regime, the August payroll release and its subsequent decay. Tail drifted between 12% and 17% through the Asian and European sessions while Stress climbed steadily into the print. The 12:30 UTC release produced the only genuine spike, with Tail reaching 24%, Stress 76% and Confidence falling to 74% as event/whipsaw mode took over. Price discovery then proved orderly: Tail decayed through 20%, 18%, 17%, 15% and 14% over the following five hourly assessments as retracements appeared and volatility fell, and the mode reverted to mixed. No hour in the window required a blocking action.
outlookSummary: The remaining cash hours are expected to keep two-sided structure with Tail in the 13-15% band, the upper end reserved for the flagged 19:00-21:00 UTC window where pre-holiday squaring can thin liquidity. US cash closes at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which the entire remainder of this horizon is a halted market with no live price path; forecast Tail therefore falls to a 4-5% closed-venue floor and the published dominant mode of normal denotes a closed venue rather than a resolved regime. Residual Stress in the 31-39% band carries what cannot price until the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, principally unresolved US-Iran hostilities and reduced Strait of Hormuz transits, and secondarily roughly 60% September Fed hike pricing. Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash session is Tuesday 8 September, and the next scheduled US data of consequence is PPI and jobless claims on Thursday 10 September followed by August CPI on Friday 11 September.
